subject.title: Plugin register() promises silently ignored — async registration not awaited

question: Should nix-openclaw align the promise-returning plugin artifacts with the existing synchronous registration contract, or should OpenClaw intentionally introduce an awaited asynchronous registration lifecycle?
rationale: Artifact alignment is a bounded packaging repair, while awaiting registration promises changes an upstream plugin API contract and startup semantics; repository evidence cannot safely choose that direction.

options.title: Align packaged artifacts
options.body: Identify and pin or patch the affected runtime-plugin artifacts so their registration follows the current synchronous OpenClaw contract.

options.title: Propose async lifecycle
options.body: Specify and approve upstream asynchronous registration semantics, including ordering, rejection handling, timeout behavior, and compatibility tests, before changing nix-openclaw pins.

recommendation.title: Align packaged artifacts
recommendation.body: Identify and pin or patch the affected runtime-plugin artifacts so their registration follows the current synchronous OpenClaw contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The best first decision point is the runtime-plugin packaging boundary, where artifact identity and revision alignment can be established before escalating upstream.
